title: Leadership and Team Management
description: Develops the leadership and teamworking competencies required at STCW management level, with a focus on the unique challenges of multinational maritime crews operating in high-stakes, remote environments. The series examines leadership styles, authority and accountability under maritime law, cross-cultural communication barriers, and the fatigue management obligations that fall on every officer in a position of authority.

title: Environmental Stewardship at Sea
description: Builds awareness and operational competence in environmental protection across pollution prevention, energy efficiency, and incident response. The series covers MARPOL obligations in daily practice, CII and SEEMP requirements for OOW energy awareness, SOPEP activation, and the Ballast Water Management Convention. Voluntary best-practice measures beyond regulatory minimums are highlighted to connect environmental responsibility with commercial and reputational value.

title: Security Awareness
description: Delivers the STCW VI/6-1 Security Awareness Training required of all seafarers under the Manila 2010 amendments, covering threat recognition, high-risk area procedures, SSAS operation, access control, and security incident reporting. The series distinguishes clearly between baseline Awareness Training and the fuller SSO certification, and provides practical guidance on applying BMP6 best management practices in piracy-prone waters.

title: Dynamic Positioning Operations
description: Provides an introduction to DP systems, positioning reference redundancy, failure modes, and the Nautical Institute certification pathway for officers working aboard DP-classed vessels. The series covers DP Class 1, 2, and 3 distinctions, FMEA requirements, operational procedures during offshore tasks including SIMOPS, and the IMCA incident reporting scheme that drives fleet-wide learning.

episodes.title: DP Sensors and Positioning Reference Systems

title: Anchor Handling Operations
description: Covers AHTS vessel operations for running and retrieving anchors for MODUs and semi-submersibles, with a strong emphasis on the deck safety hazards that make anchor handling one of the most dangerous offshore activities. Officers learn the sequence for anchor running and retrieval, the function of deck machinery including shark jaws and the stern roller, and the critical snap-back and kill-zone hazards that have caused fatalities in this sector.

title: HUET and Helicopter Survival
description: Prepares offshore seafarers for helicopter operations and underwater escape from a ditched helicopter, covering pre-flight safety briefings, the HUET pool certification exercise, and post-ditching survival priorities. The series addresses helideck safety, EBS use, capsize and exit technique, hypothermia in cold-water environments, and the SAR response timeline that determines survival outcomes.

title: Fishing Gear Operations
description: Covers the types of commercial fishing gear, their deployment and retrieval sequences, and the deck machinery safety hazards that make fishing one of the most dangerous occupations at sea. Officers and ratings learn snag and entanglement risks during hauling, the emergency stop procedures for net drums and winches, and the specific MOB dangers created by moving gear — including cold water drowning statistics for the fishing sector.

title: Catch Handling and Fish Safety
description: Addresses the stability risks of large catches on deck, the confined space atmosphere hazards in fish holds, and the cold chain and food safety requirements that govern catch quality from sea to market. Officers learn the H2S and CO2 dangers associated with fish holds, the RSW system and its maintenance, and how rapid catch processing connects directly to vessel safety through weight and free surface management.

title: Yacht Seamanship
description: Covers seamanship, weather routing, and regulatory compliance specific to commercial yachts and superyachts, including sailing yacht handling, anchoring techniques, and MCA LY3 manning requirements. Officers learn how to manage non-seafarer guests safely, apply the Commercial Endorsement rules, and navigate the intersection of charter commercial pressure and ISPS safety obligations for large yachts on international voyages.

title: Passenger Safety Management
description: Covers the STCW crowd management and crisis management training requirements for passenger ship and commercial yacht crew, including mustering non-crew passengers, directing evacuation flows, and accommodating persons with reduced mobility. The series addresses the additional MOB complexity on passenger vessels, crisis management decision-making at Master and HoD level, and the post-incident passenger welfare obligations.

episodes.title: Man Overboard on a Passenger Ship

title: Tanker Operations
description: Provides a structured introduction to tanker cargo systems, inert gas management, and the procedures for loading and discharging petroleum cargoes safely. Officers learn the IGS sequence and alarm thresholds, tank entry enclosed space requirements, crude oil washing, and the pressure surge risks at emergency shutdown. The series concludes with OCIMF SIRE 2.0 vetting inspection expectations and what a poor SIRE result means commercially.

episodes.title: Entry into Enclosed Spaces on Tankers

title: Gas Carrier Operations
description: Covers LNG and LPG cargo systems, containment types, inerting and cool-down sequences, and the management of boil-off gas, with particular attention to the cryogenic, rollover, and rapid phase transition hazards unique to gas carrier operations. Officers learn the emergency shutdown system, cargo leak response sequence, and the full STCW certification path from Basic to Advanced Training for Liquefied Gas Tankers required on their Certificate of Competency.

title: ISGOTT — International Safety Guide for Oil Tankers and Terminals
description: ISGOTT (6th edition) is the definitive safety manual for crude and product tanker operations and their interface with shore terminals. Published jointly by ICS, OCIMF, and IAPH, it is not an IMO convention but is so widely adopted that it is treated as mandatory by major charterers and terminal operators. Understanding ISGOTT is essential for any officer involved in tanker cargo operations, and it is central to SIRE 2.0 vetting inspections.

episodes.title: What is ISGOTT and How It Is Used

seasons.title: Season 3 — Gas Hazards and Hot Work

title: OCIMF SIRE 2.0 — Ship Inspection Report Programme
description: SIRE 2.0 (launched 2022) is the major overhaul of OCIMF's Ship Inspection Report Programme — the most important vetting standard for tankers. Replacing SIRE 1.0, the new version uses observation-based assessments instead of yes/no checklists, integrating human factors, safety culture evaluation, and digital reporting. A SIRE 2.0 result can determine whether a tanker gets chartered or sits idle — understanding it is commercially critical for any officer on a tanker.

title: OCIMF MEG4 — Mooring Equipment Guidelines
description: MEG4 (Mooring Equipment Guidelines, 4th edition, 2018) is OCIMF's comprehensive standard for mooring equipment design, selection, inspection, and operation. It replaced MEG3 to address the rising fatality rate from mooring failures and snapback incidents. MEG4 is referenced in SIRE, CDI, and RightShip vetting inspections, and many flag states and terminal operators require MEG4-compliant mooring equipment and procedures.

title: OCIMF OSV Recommendations
description: OCIMF's recommendations for Offshore Support Vessels cover design and construction guidelines, manning, and operational procedures for Platform Supply Vessels (PSV), Anchor Handling Tug Supply vessels (AHTS), and Emergency Response and Rescue Vessels (ERRV). While not binding in the way of IMO conventions, these guidelines are referenced in OVID vetting and by major oil company operators. Understanding OCIMF OSV standards is essential for officers working in the offshore support sector.

title: OCIMF TMSA — Tanker Management and Self Assessment
description: TMSA (Tanker Management and Self Assessment) is OCIMF's framework for assessing a shipping company's safety management system. Companies submit annual self-assessments against 12 Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), each with 4 stages of performance. TMSA scores are submitted to OCIMF and shared with charterers who use them as part of their approval process. Understanding TMSA is essential for shore-based managers and senior officers who want to understand the commercial safety expectations of the oil major charterers.

title: CDI — Chemical Tanker Inspection Scheme
description: The CDI (Chemical Distribution Institute) Marine inspection scheme is the chemical tanker equivalent of OCIMF SIRE. CDI inspections verify a chemical tanker's compliance with the IBC Code, MARPOL Annex II, and cargo operator requirements. CDI reports are stored in a database accessible to cargo owners and charterers, and a poor CDI result can prevent a chemical tanker from loading for major shippers. CDI is distinct from SIRE and covers aspects of chemical tanker operations not addressed in the oil tanker vetting framework.

title: OPITO BOSIET — Basic Offshore Safety Induction and Emergency Training
description: BOSIET (Basic Offshore Safety Induction and Emergency Training) is the mandatory safety certification for everyone who works offshore, whether on platforms, FPSOs, or offshore support vessels. Issued under the OPITO (Offshore Petroleum Industry Training Organization) standard, it covers sea survival, firefighting, first aid, and helicopter underwater escape training (HUET). BOSIET is typically required before a first offshore trip and must be renewed every 4 years (FOET refresher).

episodes.title: What is BOSIET and Who Needs It

title: OPITO HUET — Helicopter Underwater Escape Training
description: OPITO HUET (Helicopter Underwater Escape Training) is the standalone version of the underwater escape component of BOSIET for workers who already hold the full BOSIET certificate and need to maintain the helicopter escape skill. HUET trains participants to exit a simulated helicopter cabin after it inverts and sinks — the scenario in an offshore helicopter ditching. The training is physically demanding and must be renewed as part of the FOET cycle. Understanding HUET requirements and procedures is essential for any seafarer working in an offshore helicopter-served environment.

title: DP Operator Certificate (Nautical Institute)
description: The Nautical Institute DP Operator Certificate is the global standard for certification of Dynamic Positioning officers. While not an IMO convention requirement (STCW V/3 references it), the NI DP Certificate is required by virtually all major offshore operators and is specified in every DP vessel charter party. The certificate has two levels: DP Limited (for vessels in limited operations with DP1/2) and DP Unlimited (for all DP operations including deepwater DP3). Understanding the NI DP certificate path is essential for any officer planning an offshore career.

title: ICS Bridge Procedures Guide
description: The ICS Bridge Procedures Guide (6th edition) is the most widely used practical reference for shipboard navigation procedures and bridge team management. Published by the International Chamber of Shipping, it is not a mandatory regulation but is used as the industry standard for developing company-specific bridge procedures manuals. Port State Control inspectors, vetting inspectors, and accident investigators routinely reference the ICS Bridge Procedures Guide when evaluating a ship's navigational safety culture.

title: ICS Tanker Safety Guide
description: The ICS Tanker Safety Guide (Liquefied Gas, Chemicals, or Oil — separate volumes) provides comprehensive guidance for safe tanker operations, complementing ISGOTT and the MARPOL/IBC/IGC regulatory framework. Published by ICS in conjunction with OCIMF, these guides cover everything from pre-arrival planning to emergency procedures specific to tanker cargo types. They are referenced in SIRE and CDI vetting and form the basis for many company SMS procedures on tanker fleets.

episodes.title: Using ICS Guides in SMS Development

title: RightShip GHG Rating
description: RightShip is an independent maritime risk assessment company whose vetting services are used extensively by dry bulk charterers (BHP, Rio Tinto, etc.) and some container operators. The RightShip GHG Rating (A-G scale) assesses a vessel's carbon efficiency relative to comparable ships and is increasingly used in chartering decisions alongside the IMO CII rating. Ships with a poor RightShip GHG rating or low safety score face reduced chartering opportunities in the dry bulk and bulk liquid sectors.

title: IMCA DP Standards
description: IMCA (International Marine Contractors Association) is the body that sets industry standards for offshore marine operations, particularly DP. IMCA documents (M 103, M 117, M 190, D 007) govern DP vessel capability assessments, incident reporting, operations guidance, and competence standards. Compliance with IMCA DP standards is required by oil majors, offshore operators, and insurers. IMCA M 117 (DP incident reporting) is the most widely cited document in the offshore industry's safety learning system.

title: OCIMF OVID — Offshore Vessel Inspection Database
description: OCIMF OVID (Offshore Vessel Inspection Database) is the offshore equivalent of the SIRE tanker vetting database. OVID stores inspection reports for offshore support vessels — PSVs, AHTSs, ERRVs — conducted against the OCIMF/IMCA Offshore Vessel Inspection Questionnaire (OVIQ). Oil company operators use OVID results when approving offshore support vessels for charter. An OVID inspection covers vessel condition, safety systems, DP capability, crew competence, and compliance with OCIMF OSV recommendations and IMCA standards.

episodes.title: OVID and SIRE on the Same Vessel
